findings.issue_text: Team authorization requires a user to be both an admin and an owner (`&&`), incorrectly denying team admins access; it should use an OR check.
Blacklist entries are lowercased but submitted guest emails are not, allowing blacklist bypasses through case variations.
The API schema does not enforce unique guest emails, allowing duplicate attendee records.
Email dispatch uses the original `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so existing attendees can be misclassified as newly added and receive a new-booking confirmation.

Attendees are persisted before calendar updates and email notifications; if the calendar update fails, database changes remain and retries fail because guests already exist, leaving systems out of sync.

Calendar updates use the current caller’s credentials instead of the booking organizer’s credentials, so authorized attendees or team admins may update through—or fail against—the wrong calendar account.

Team members never receive the intended notification because the booking query does not load team members and the constructed `CalendarEvent` does not set `team`, leaving `calendarEvent.team?.members` absent.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees are persisted before calendar updates and email notifications; if the calendar update fails, database changes remain and retries fail because guests already exist, leaving systems out of sync.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the code flow is: 1) prisma.booking.update creates attendees in DB (lines 89-103), 2) eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees updates calendar (line 161), 3) sendAddGuestsEmails sends notifications (line 165). If updateCalendarAttendees fails after the DB update, the attendees are already persisted. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) would filter out already-added guests since they now exist in booking.attendees, potentially resulting in an empty list and throwing 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This leaves the database and calendar out of sync with no clean recovery path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar updates use the current caller’s credentials instead of the booking organizer’s credentials, so authorized attendees or team admins may update through—or fail against—the wrong calendar account.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, line 161-165 shows `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and then `new EventManager({...user, credentials: [...credentials]})`. The ctx.user is the current caller (who could be an attendee or team admin per the permission check on lines 47-53), not the booking organizer. The booking organizer's credentials are fetched in the booking query (line 38-39 includes user.credentials) but never used. This means calendar updates will use the wrong credentials when an attendee or team admin adds guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team members never receive the intended notification because the booking query does not load team members and the constructed `CalendarEvent` does not set `team`, leaving `calendarEvent.team?.members` absent.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the booking query includes eventType, attendees, references, user, and destinationCalendar, but does NOT include team or team members. When constructing the CalendarEvent (evt), there is no 'team' property being set. In email-manager.ts, sendAddGuestsEmails checks `calendarEvent.team?.members` to send emails to team members, but since team is never populated in the evt object, this loop will never execute. This is a real bug where team members won't receive notifications about added guests.
